dependencies.reason: Removes obsolete packages (compaction, session, middleware, stop), cleans up dead tools, and renames module.
Rewrites provider/anthropic over official SDK, provides anthropic.Resolve, Claude catalog.Lookup, Effort, strict tool declarations, and cache breakpoints.
Provides ReachableTools, NestedCaller, and wrapper resolution semantics for batch execution.
Provides Starlark code mode tool which executes nested tool calls and depends on interceptor error values.

tasks.title: Implement driver configuration, constructor validation, and eager shell tool guard checks
steps: Define Config struct in agentkit with Client, Provider, Model, Effort, System, Prefix, Tools, Policy, Guard, After, MaxTurns, MaxCostUSD, Timeout, Prune, and MaxTokens.
Implement New(cfg Config) (*Agent, error) rejecting configurations where both cfg.Client and cfg.Provider are nil.
In New, validate that cfg.Model is non-empty, returning an error naming the missing model identifier.
In New, validate the tool hierarchy: check that each tool specifies exactly one of Handler or Execute, detect reachability cycles, and reject wrappers reaching Terminating tools.
In New, resolve active tools using cfg.Policy.Resolve(cfg.Tools), and prioritize cfg.Provider over cfg.Client for request dispatch.

In New, eagerly inspect resolved and transitively reachable tools for shell tools using guard.IsShellTool; if any shell tool is reachable and cfg.Guard is nil, return fmt.Errorf("%w (tool %q)", core.ErrUnguardedExecute, toolName) or fmt.Errorf("%w (wrapper %q reached shell tool %q)", core.ErrUnguardedExecute, wrapperName, shellToolName).
Write and verify unit tests TS-11-1 through TS-11-8 covering configuration fields, constructor rejections, tool resolution, and eager shell guard validation.

tasks.title: Implement consumer execution surface and Agent concurrency control
steps: Restrict the exported method set of Agent solely to Run, Stream, Messages, Usage, and ReachableTools.
Implement single-execution concurrency control on Agent, rejecting overlapping calls to Run or Stream with core.ErrBusy.
Implement safe concurrent reads of Messages(), Usage(), and ReachableTools() while execution is actively in flight.
Implement Agent.Run(ctx, prompt) to run the minimal loop to a stop condition and return core.RunResult with transcript, usage, turns, and stop reason.
Implement Agent.Stream(ctx, prompt) to execute the driver loop asynchronously and return *core.EventStream without blocking loop execution.
Write and verify tests TS-11-9 through TS-11-13 covering surface restriction, Run execution, Stream non-blocking delivery, ErrBusy rejection, and race-free state inspection.

tasks.title: Implement prompt guideline assembly, prefix messages, and cache breakpoints
steps: Assemble the system prompt for outbound requests using prompt.Build(cfg.System, resolvedTools), deduplicating PromptGuidelines in first-seen order.
Prepend cfg.Prefix messages before the user prompt and conversation history on all outbound requests.
Stamp an ephemeral cache control breakpoint on the final content block of the assembled system prompt.
Stamp an ephemeral cache control breakpoint on the final tool definition in the active tool list if tools are present.
Stamp an ephemeral cache control breakpoint on the final content block of cfg.Prefix when prefix messages exist.
Stamp an ephemeral cache control breakpoint on the final content block of the most recent outbound user message.
Write and verify unit tests TS-11-14 through TS-11-16 covering guideline assembly, prefix ordering, and four-point ephemeral cache breakpoints.

tasks.title: Implement outbound context pruning and context window overflow enforcement
steps: Define PruneOptions struct with Threshold float64 and KeepTurns int fields.
Implement anchored token estimation using the latest assistant usage report plus 4 characters per token for subsequent messages, falling back to 4 chars/token over the entire view if unanchored.

When cfg.Prune.Threshold > 0 and estimated tokens divided by the model context window from catalog.Lookup(cfg.Model) meets or exceeds Threshold, replace tool result bodies older than currentTurn - KeepTurns with the elision notice stating tool name and original byte length.
Ensure outbound view pruning strictly preserves ToolResultMessage.ToolUseID pairing with corresponding assistant ToolUseBlock.ID.
Ensure the durable transcript returned by Messages() and RunResult.Messages remains unmodified and intact during pruning.
If estimated tokens exceed the catalog model context window capacity after pruning, terminate the run immediately with RunStopError and an error naming the model and context window capacity.
Write and verify tests TS-11-17 through TS-11-21 covering PruneOptions, outbound result elision, ID pairing, transcript durability, and context window limit termination.

tasks.title: Implement turn continuation logic, synthetic truncation handling, and stop conditions
steps: Evaluate turn continuation exclusively by checking whether the assistant message contains one or more ToolUseBlock elements, ignoring StopReason.
When an assistant message contains ToolUseBlock elements and StopReason is StopReasonLength, skip tool handler execution for all calls in the batch.

For truncated batches under StopReasonLength, append a synthetic ToolResultMessage to each call stating the fixed notice that the call was not executed due to output token limit truncation and to re-issue with complete arguments.
Append synthetic truncation results to the transcript and continue the loop to the next turn without terminating the run.
When an assistant message contains no ToolUseBlock elements and StopReason is StopReasonRefusal, terminate the run with RunStopRefusal and core.ErrRefusal.
When an assistant message contains no ToolUseBlock elements and no error or refusal, complete the run normally with RunStopEndTurn.
Write and verify unit tests TS-11-22 through TS-11-25 covering tool-based turn continuation, synthetic truncation handling, refusal termination, and normal turn completion.

tasks.title: Implement batch tool execution pipeline and batch termination voting
steps: Implement Phase 1 (Prepare): sequentially validate arguments with core.PrepareArguments and evaluate Config.Guard on the loop goroutine, immediately finalizing invalid or blocked calls as error results without invoking handlers.

Implement Phase 2 (Abort Decision): evaluate ctx.Err() once before handlers spawn; if context is cancelled, mark all remaining unfinalized calls aborted without starting handlers; if active, proceed to Phase 3.

Implement Phase 3 (Execute): run tool handlers concurrently using one goroutine per call joined by sync.WaitGroup (never errgroup); if any tool is marked Sequential or ParallelTools is disabled, execute handlers sequentially in call order.
Implement Phase 4 (Finalize): serialize Config.After callbacks and event emission under a batch-scoped mutex, placing results into slot index order so transcript order matches assistant call order.
Implement batch termination voting: when an executed handler returns Terminate: true, allow sibling calls in the batch to complete, then terminate the run with RunStopToolTerminate.
Ensure Phase 1 validation errors and guard rejections do not trigger RunStopToolTerminate.

Write and verify unit tests TS-11-26 through TS-11-32 covering Phase 1 prepare and guard rejection, Phase 2 abort evaluation, Phase 3 concurrency, Phase 4 slot-indexed ordering, batch termination voting, and no termination on blocked calls.

tasks.title: Implement nested tool execution pipeline for wrapper tools
steps: In batch execution, when executing a tool with ReachableTools, construct a nestedCaller and attach core.NestedCaller to the handler's execution context.
In NestedCaller.Call, enforce reachability: reject tool calls outside the wrapper's resolved reachable set with an error ToolResult (IsError: true).
In NestedCaller.Call, emit execution events populated with ParentToolUseID matching the parent wrapper tool call ID.
When a nested call is blocked by a BeforeToolCall interceptor, return an error ToolResult with a nil Go error to allow wrapper scripts to inspect the rejection.
If an interceptor votes to terminate during a nested call, reject subsequent nested calls with core.ErrTerminated and propagate the termination vote to the parent wrapper result.

Write and verify unit tests TS-11-33 through TS-11-37 covering nested caller attachment, reachable set enforcement, parent event attribution, interceptor error values with nil Go error, and termination propagation.

tasks.title: Implement run bounds, limits, panic recovery, and stream resilience
steps: When Config.Timeout > 0, derive run context with context.WithTimeout; terminate with RunStopTimeout if the deadline expires.
When Config.MaxTurns > 0 and turn count reaches MaxTurns, terminate the run with RunStopMaxTurns and core.ErrMaxTurns.

When Config.MaxCostUSD > 0, check accumulated model usage cost before issuing each request; terminate before request dispatch with RunStopBudgetExceeded and core.ErrBudgetExceeded if cost meets or exceeds MaxCostUSD.
When the run context is cancelled externally between turns without timeout expiration, terminate the run with RunStopAborted and core.ErrAborted.
Implement panic recovery around tool handlers, interceptors, and hooks: catch panics, convert to error ToolResultMessage, emit an error event, and keep the process alive.
Ensure *core.EventStream buffers and drops unread events according to StreamOptions without blocking loop goroutine execution on slow or detached consumers.
Write and verify unit tests TS-11-38 through TS-11-43 covering timeout expiration, turn limits, budget limits, external abort, panic recovery, and non-blocking event streaming.

tasks.title: Verify all driver execution paths end to end with smoke tests
steps: Implement and verify smoke test TS-11-44 for 11-PATH-1: multi-turn prompt execution with concurrent tool batch.
Implement and verify smoke test TS-11-45 for 11-PATH-2: outbound context pruning under token threshold pressure with durable transcript preservation.
Implement and verify smoke test TS-11-46 for 11-PATH-3: synthetic truncation recovery on max_tokens response with complete arguments re-issue.
Implement and verify smoke test TS-11-47 for 11-PATH-4: nested tool execution through wrapper tool with parent event attribution.
Implement and verify smoke test TS-11-48 for 11-PATH-5: eager shell tool guard enforcement rejection at construction.
Implement and verify smoke test TS-11-49 for 11-PATH-6: run termination on budget limit exceeded before outbound request dispatch.
Trace every execution path (11-PATH-1 through 11-PATH-6) through the real code in Agent, New, runLoop, executeBatch, and nestedCaller; confirm each step calls the next and no stub remains.

For every criterion with a contract (11-REQ-1.2, 11-REQ-1.3, 11-REQ-1.4, 11-REQ-1.5, 11-REQ-2.1, 11-REQ-2.2, 11-REQ-2.3, 11-REQ-3.2, 11-REQ-3.3, 11-REQ-3.4, 11-REQ-5.5, 11-REQ-6.4, 11-REQ-6.5, 11-REQ-8.1, 11-REQ-8.3, 11-REQ-9.2, 11-REQ-9.4, 11-REQ-9.5, 11-REQ-10.1, 11-REQ-10.2, 11-REQ-10.3, 11-REQ-10.4, 11-REQ-10.5), confirm the producer's result is consumed by a caller in production code.
Search touched files for stub markers ('TODO', 'panic(\"not implemented\")', bare returns on non-trivial paths) and confirm none remain.
